| Scene description | • The site is busy Jianghan Road Food Street, Jianghan District, with food stalls and temporary collection facilities.<br>• S14-B-01 shows an uncovered white crate containing foam containers, bags and food scraps beside scooters and tactile paving.<br>• S14-B-04 shows a stained, open metal bin with a classification slogan beside stalls, with a little litter beneath.<br>• S14-B-05 shows two stained, open classification bins against a wall, an orange plastic box of cardboard tubes, slippery ground and standing water, with scooters and brooms nearby. The evening or night-time dining area shows improperly used facilities, spills or accumulation. |
| Regulatory basis | • Jianghan District urban management enforcement departments are responsible for pedestrian-street sanitation, including maintenance and supervision of collection facilities. Wuhan Municipal Provisions on the Management of the Jianghan Road Pedestrian Street Area, Article 15, [D-15-C004](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering or stockpiling requires correction and penalties: CNY 5,000–50,000 for organisations and up to CNY 200 for individuals. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 42, [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Collection facilities should be properly installed, lidded and regularly cleaned to prevent spills and accumulation and meet technical and sanitation standards. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 16, Article 42, [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Responsible parties on Jianghan Road should sign frontage responsibility agreements, fulfil sanitation duties and accept subdistrict or urban-management supervision. Wuhan Municipal Measures for the Three Responsibilities in Front of Premises, Article 11, [D-09-C006](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Unauthorised commercial waste cleaning, collection, transport or disposal must cease and attracts a CNY 30,000 fine. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 43, [D-03-C008](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Two accumulations and four non-overflowing but poorly managed collection points show spills, stains, litter and standing water. These management shortcomings affect sanitation and pedestrian safety in a busy food street. |
| Impact assessment | Visible effects include litter, stained bins and slippery, waterlogged ground, with potential falls, insects and odours. Near-term risks in this busy food street include greater accumulation, visual impacts, complaints and sanitation or safety problems. |
| Potential causes | • Vendors or businesses may delay collection or use bins improperly: the uncovered S14-B-01 crate contains food scraps and the non-standard S14-B-05 box contains tubes.<br>• Facility maintenance may be delayed: S14-B-04 and S14-B-05 bins are stained and open.<br>• Frontage responsibilities may be unfulfilled. Verify agreements, supervision and penalty records.<br>• Evening or night collection may be inadequate. Check collection schedules against business peaks. |
| Long-term effects | Persistent or recurrent problems could normalise accumulation, intensify insects and odours, cause pedestrian avoidance or complaints, harm Jianghan Road’s image and visitor experience, and trigger enforcement and higher management costs. |
| Recommendations | • Immediate action: clear S14-B-01, S14-B-04 and S14-B-05 litter and standing water, wash and cover bins, and replace non-standard crates and boxes with properly provided containers.<br>• Longer-term action: enforce frontage responsibilities, train businesses in classification and sanitation, optimise collection after evening dining peaks, undertake regular checks, publicise violations and establish incentives and penalties. |
| Priority | **High.** Accumulation and spills in a busy dining street create immediate risks from slippery ground, odours and insects. Prompt action is needed to prevent deterioration in this priority enforcement area. |
